subtitle: How Shivaji Forged a Language and Law of Swarajya

panels.shot: low-angle wide of Raigad durbar under monsoon clouds
panels.action: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj stands in full rajabhishek regalia in the Raigad hall, eight ministerial seats receding behind him, while a scribe unfurls a palm-leaf manuscript at his side.

dialogue.text: After the sword was sheathed at Raigad, Shivaji faced a quieter battle: how to bind a new kingdom with law, language and eight ministers instead of chains.

i18n.hi: रायगड पर तलवार म्यान हुई, तो शिवाजी के सामने नई जंग थी – जंजीरों नहीं, कानून, भाषा और आठ मंत्रियों से राज्य बांधने की।

panels.shot: slow push-in from balcony over Raigad into distant valleys
panels.action: Shivaji leans on the carved stone balustrade of Raigad’s terrace at dawn, looking over mist-filled valleys and scattered forts, a scroll in his hand and worry in his eyes.

dialogue.text: By 1674, forts from Konkan to the ghats flew his standard, yet the lands beneath were a patchwork of habits, dues and tongues still echoing older sultanates.

i18n.hi: १६७४ तक कोंकण से घाटों तक किले उस का भगवा फहरा रहे थे, पर नीचे की धरती अभी भी पुराने सुल्तानों की रीत, लगान और बोलियों का जाल थी।

panels.shot: high-angle interior of council hall, symmetrical composition
panels.action: Inside the Raigad audience hall, Shivaji sits firmly on the throne while eight empty but ornate seats form a semicircle before him, attendants laying down carpets and ledgers.

dialogue.text: To hold Swarajya together, he turned the war council into a state council, the famed Ashtapradhan—eight chief ministers to share power and burden.

i18n.hi: स्वराज्य जोड़े रखने को उस ने युद्ध–दरबार को राज–दरबार बनाया – मशहूर ‘अष्टप्रधान’, आठ मंत्री जो ताकत और बोझ बाँटें।

panels.shot: medium frontal shot of Shivaji addressing assembled court
panels.action: Shivaji, seated but leaning forward with intent, gestures towards the eight seats now occupied by dignified ministers, each with distinctive scrolls, swords or beads.

dialogue.text: The Peshwa would steer policy, the Amatya weigh the treasury, the Sachiv guard state letters, and the Sumant handle foreign courts and war councils.

i18n.hi: पेशवा नीति चलाए, अमात्य खजाना तौले, सचिव राजपत्र संभाले और सुमंत विदेश दरबारों व युद्ध–सभाओं से निपटे।

panels.action: The view glides past the stern Senapati with a campaign map, the Mantri with a chronicle in hand, the composed Nyayadhish listening, and the Panditrao fingering a rosary beside donation records.

dialogue.text: The Senapati would marshal arms, the Mantri record glory and failure, the Nyayadhish guard justice, and the Panditrao oversee grants and sacred trusts.

i18n.hi: सेनापति हथियारों की फौज सँभाले, मंत्री बखान और नाकामी लिखे, न्यायाधीश न्याय की रखवाली करे, पंडितराव दान और देवधन देखें।

panels.shot: close-up on Shivaji’s face, half lit by window light
panels.action: A close profile of Shivaji shows him listening as a clerk murmurs in Persian, another in Modi script; he raises a hand, eyes narrowing in thought.

dialogue.text: Yet in his halls, Persian farmans and Marathi petitions jostled on the same floor. Words themselves were divided—kingdom in two scripts, two idioms.

i18n.hi: पर दरबार में फ़ारसी फरमान और मराठी अर्जियाँ एक ही फ़र्श पर टकराती रहीं – खुद शब्द बँटे थे, एक राज्य दो लिपियों, दो बोलियों में।

panels.shot: over-the-shoulder of a scribe in a dim study
panels.action: In a quiet chamber lined with palm leaves, the scholar Raghunath Pandit bends over a desk, carefully inscribing neat columns of Sanskrit and Marathi terms on a long manuscript.

dialogue.text: So he entrusted a pandit, Raghunath by name, to weave a lexicon of rule—the Rajya Vyavahara Kosha, a treasury of 1,344 words binding Sanskrit and Marathi to statecraft.

i18n.hi: तब उसने पंडित रघुनाथ को जिम्मा दिया – राजव्यवहार कोश रचने का, १,३४४ शब्दों का खज़ाना जो संस्कृत–मराठी को राजकाज से बाँधे।

panels.shot: macro close-up of palm-leaf manuscript surface
panels.action: Extreme close-up shows incised letters on a palm leaf: old Persianate court terms scratched out beside newly coined Sanskrit-Marathi equivalents, with a stylus resting between lines.

dialogue.text: Where older courts said ‘farman’ and ‘huzur’, the Kosha set down ‘adesh’ and ‘rajadhiraj’. It did not bar Persian, but gave Swarajya its own tongue of command.

i18n.hi: जहाँ पुराने दरबार ‘फरमान’ और ‘हुज़ूर’ कहते थे, कोश ने ‘आदेश’ और ‘राजाधिराज’ जमाया। फ़ारसी रोकी नहीं, बस स्वराज्य को अपनी हुक्म की ज़ुबान दी।

panels.shot: medium shot of Shivaji examining the manuscript with scholars
panels.action: Shivaji sits at a low desk flanked by Brahmin scholars and a Muslim karkun; he runs his finger over the manuscript, nodding as the others watch with quiet curiosity.

dialogue.speaker: chhatrapati_shivaji_maharaj
dialogue.text: Let our orders speak in the people’s words, yet be understood in every court.

i18n.hi: “हमारे हुक्म जनता की बोली में हों, मगर हर दरबार में समझे जाएँ।”

panels.shot: wide shot of revenue officers in a Konkan village field
panels.action: In a Konkan village, state karkuns in simple turbans pace along a rope stretched across a field, measuring with bamboo rods as farmers look on, palm-leaf records tied at their waists.

dialogue.text: On the ground, Shivaji’s men measured field after field, following the lines laid by Malik Ambar before them, turning scattered dues into coherent assessment.

i18n.hi: ज़मीन पर शिवाजी के कारिंदे खेत–दर–खेत नापते चले, मलिक अंबर के पुराने नक्शे पर चलकर बिखरे लगान को ठोस बंदोबस्त में बदला।

panels.shot: medium shot of a karkun recording while farmer gestures to his land
panels.action: A Konkan farmer points earnestly to a patch of land while a karkun squats, writing in Modi script with calm concentration, another clerk holding a wooden measuring rod upright.

dialogue.text: The state leaned less on hereditary middlemen and more on its own karkuns, bargaining and recording in village courtyards instead of only in distant forts.

i18n.hi: राज अब वंशानुगत मझदारों पर कम, अपने कारकुनों पर ज़्यादा टिकने लगा – सौदे और लेखा किले से ज़्यादा गाँव की चौपालों में होने लगे।

panels.shot: interior medium shot of Shivaji dictating to a Persian and Marathi scribe
panels.action: In a Raigad office, Shivaji sits cross-legged, dictating calmly while one scribe writes in Persian and another in Marathi; behind them, a shelf of neatly bound farmans stands.

dialogue.text: Some orders still flowed in Persian for old allies, others in Marathi for new subjects. The Kosha gave both a bridge, not a wall.

i18n.hi: कुछ हुक्म पुराने यारों के लिए अब भी फ़ारसी में, कुछ नए प्रजाजनों के लिए मराठी में – कोश ने दोनों के बीच दीवार नहीं, पुल खड़ा किया।

panels.shot: medium shot of a Muslim officer reading a royal order in a mosque courtyard
panels.action: In a small mosque courtyard, a bearded officer in Deccan attire reads a palm-leaf order to assembled townsfolk; the mosque stands serene behind, its arches framing the scene.

dialogue.text: Among those who carried these words were men like Siddi Ibrahim and Ibrahim Khan, Muslim captains who stood under the same Bhagwa standard in battle and in pay lists.

i18n.hi: इन शब्दों को ढोने वालों में सिद्दी इब्राहीम और इब्राहीम ख़ान जैसे मुसलमान सरदार भी थे, जो वही भगवा झंडा लेकर लड़ते और वही वेतन लेते थे।

panels.shot: overhead view of a royal order being sealed in the chancery
panels.action: A royal clerk presses a seal into a freshly folded order on a wooden table; beside the text, an Arabic mention of Quran and a Marathi line about protection can be seen in delicate script.

dialogue.text: In farmans now preserved in archives, Shivaji’s seal endorses orders forbidding harm to mosques and Qurans, commands that troops guard, not defile, houses of prayer.

i18n.hi: आज जो फरमान खज़ानों में हैं, उन पर शिवाजी की मुहर है – मस्जिदों और क़ुरान को छूने की मनाही, फौज को इबादतगाहें बचाने, न बिगाड़ने का हुक्म।

panels.shot: wide shot of soldiers passing peacefully by a mosque and houses
panels.action: A column of Maratha soldiers marches through a town street, glancing respectfully at a mosque and homes; a local family watches from a doorway, anxious faces easing as the troops pass without disturbance.

dialogue.text: Orders also ran ahead of armies—no harassing women, no plundering peasants, no burning fields without need. Not always obeyed, but written, and repeated.

i18n.hi: हुक्म सेनाओं से आगे निकलते – औरतों को मत सताओ, किसानों को मत लूटो, बेकार खेत मत जलाओ; हर बार नहीं माना गया, पर लिखा गया, दोहराया गया।

panels.shot: interior court scene with Nyayadhish presiding and Shivaji observing discreetly
panels.action: In a Raigad judicial hall, the Nyayadhish sits upright on a low platform hearing a land dispute, while Shivaji watches from a side seat, silent and expressionless, hands clasped.

dialogue.text: Justice, too, was drawn from layered sources—old village custom, Deccan practice, dharmashastra—and filtered through a Nyayadhish meant to stand even before the king.

i18n.hi: न्याय भी कई धाराओं से आता – गाँव की रीत, दकनी चलन, धर्मशास्त्र – और एक न्यायाधीश से होकर गुजरता जो राजा के सामने भी टिकने को बनाया गया था।

panels.shot: close-up on a villager’s anxious face in court, then on Nyayadhish’s steady gaze
panels.action: A poor villager stands wringing his hands as he speaks, eyes fearful; opposite him, the Nyayadhish listens with steady gaze, a clerk beside him noting every word.

dialogue.text: Bakhars remember instances where even royal officers were fined. Whether all such tales are exact or not, they mark the ideal: law above rank.

i18n.hi: बखरों में किस्से हैं कि राज–अधिकारी तक पर जुर्माना लगा। कहानी पूरी सही हो या नहीं, उसूल साफ दिखता है – कानून, पद से ऊपर।

panels.shot: dim archival room, modern historian studying the Rajya Vyavahara Kosha
panels.action: Centuries later in a Pune archive, a historian in simple shirt and spectacles bends under lamplight over the Rajya Vyavahara Kosha, gloved hands gently turning a fragile leaf.

dialogue.text: Today, that Kosha survives as brittle leaves in archives—evidence that Swarajya’s glory was not merely in raids and sieges, but in a grammar of governance.

i18n.hi: आज वही कोश अर्काइव में नाज़ुक पन्नों पर बचा है – यह दिखाने कि स्वराज्य की शान सिर्फ धावे और घेरों में नहीं, राजकाज की व्याकरण में भी थी।

panels.shot: wide, slightly low-angle shot of Shivaji walking through Raigad offices
panels.action: Shivaji walks through a Raigad corridor lined with busy clerks, survey maps and bound volumes; he pauses, resting his hand on a stack of ledgers as if on a sword-hilt, face calm and resolved.

dialogue.text: In the end, this was his quieter conquest: eight ministers, measured fields, protected shrines and a shared language of orders, making a state that tried to outlive the man who forged it.

i18n.hi: आख़िर यही उसकी खामोश जीत थी – आठ मंत्री, नापी हुई ज़मीनें, बची हुई पूजा–स्थलियाँ और एक साझी हुक्म–ज़ुबान, जिसने उस आदमी से आगे तक रहने वाला राज्य गढ़ने की कोशिश की।

title_i18n.en: Eight Ministers and the Kosha of Rule

subtitle_i18n.en: How Shivaji Forged a Language and Law of Swarajya
